summary:
**Space Facts Game – Learn Space While You Play!**

Space Facts Game is an interactive educational rocket game developed by Team Rocket Raccoons using Scratch on PictoBlox for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

The game aims to make space exploration and mission-related learning fun and accessible for beginners. Players control a rocket travelling through space, collecting stars to increase their scores. For every 10 points earned, a new space fact is unlocked, rewarding players with interesting knowledge about our universe. For example, players discover fascinating facts such as a day on Venus being longer than a year on Venus.

Inspired by educational resources, quizzes and digital activities from the Canadian Space Agency, our project combines simple gameplay with interactive learning.

The project addresses the challenge by introducing students to space concepts through hands-on digital gaming. As a future enhancement, we plan to introduce rocket, fuel and budget choices to demonstrate the real-world trade-offs involved in designing space missions.

Our vision is simple: **Make space learning exciting, interactive and accessible to everyone!**
details:
Project Name: Space Facts Game

Team: Rocket Raccoons
Challenge: Space Mission Design Game
Team Members: Aadhinath S.V. Nair and Rithu Krishna S.V. Nair
Technology: Scratch on PictoBlox

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

Space Facts Game is an interactive educational rocket game designed to make learning about space exciting and accessible to beginners. Players control a rocket travelling through space and collect stars to increase their scores. Every time they reach 10 points, they unlock a reward in the form of an interesting space fact. This creates a fun learning experience where gameplay and space education go hand in hand.

2. What benefits does it offer?

The game introduces children and beginners to fascinating space concepts without requiring prior knowledge of astronomy or space science. It encourages curiosity, active participation and learning through exploration rather than traditional methods of memorisation.

3. What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to make space education more engaging and accessible, especially for young learners. By combining gaming with scientific facts, we hope to inspire more students to explore space science, technology and future space missions.

4. What tools and technologies were used?

The game was developed using Scratch-based visual programming on PictoBlox. We also referred to educational resources, including space quizzes, digital games and e-books from the Canadian Space Agency.

5. How is the project creative?

The creative element is the combination of a simple rocket adventure with a reward-based educational system. Instead of simply presenting facts, the game encourages players to discover them by collecting stars and achieving scores. Every 10 points creates a new learning opportunity.

6. What factors did the team consider?

We focused on:

  • Accessibility: Making the game simple enough for beginners.
  • Engagement: Using rocket movement, star collection and scoring to maintain interest.
  • Learning: Presenting space facts as rewards.
  • Simplicity: Avoiding complex scientific terminology so children can enjoy learning.
  • Future development: Planning to introduce rocket selection, fuel and budget choices to demonstrate the real-world trade-offs involved in space mission design.

Our vision is to make space exploration concepts easier to understand through interactive learning and creativity.
